lots.what_it_is: Hine X.O. Cognac figural porcelain decanter (catalogued by Gowans as 'HINE LIMOGES COGNAC DECANTER'), cobalt blue glaze, reclining stag with silvered antlers on a rectangular plinth with gilt 'X.O. HINE COGNAC' wreath panel. Same mould as the Hine stag decanters sold by Scotch Whisky Auctions, but this is the blue X.O. version. The filler neck at front left is open with no stopper in the photo, so it is probably empty.

Hammer only (winning bid). Rate AUD 1.907 per GBP (open.er-api.com, 1 Oct 2026). Category guide only, cannot set a bid.

No unsold or asking evidence found.

lots.question_for_gowans: Is the decanter empty or does it still hold cognac? Is the stopper present? Any chips or repairs to the antlers or glaze, and is there a Limoges or maker's mark on the base?

lots.what_it_is: Brown leather officer's Sam Browne belt (waist belt only, no cross strap shown) with a double-tongue brass buckle, D-rings, a brass sword-frog hook, a stud, and brass rosette studs at the brace attachments, with decorative stitching. Gowans title: WWI Tasmanian officer's belt of Capt (later Col) W H Gray, 26th Bn, 7th Brigade AIF, by J Fotheringham of Launceston. The maker and name are NOT visible in any photo; the attribution rests on a printed seller sheet.
lots.guide_summary: No SOLD, UNSOLD or ASKING evidence found. WebSearch was unavailable (session budget used up) and a Grays search for 'sam browne belt' returned no usable results. No price range can be given.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep and flip maximums are both 0.
lots.confidence_reason: No price evidence at all. The maker's stamp and the officer's name the sheet says 'remain legible' are not shown in any photo, so the provenance is unverified.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 1: whole belt beside the printed sheet. Photo 2: outer face with stitched decoration, two D-ring brace attachments each with two brass rosette (rose-pattern) studs, a brass frog hook, a brass stud and a double-tongue brass buckle. Photo 3: the printed A4 sheet. No photo of the inside of the belt, so the claimed stamp and name are not seen. No cross strap. The sheet reads like generic sales copy and has internal inconsistencies: it says Gray was 'commissioned as a Lieutenant' in 1913, and also that he enlisted as a Second Lieutenant in June 1915 and was promoted Lieutenant at Gallipoli; Gowans' title says 'later Colonel' while the sheet's main text says Captain; and there is a stray '[1]' citation marker. Rose-pattern studs are fairly common on officer pattern belts, so they do not on their own support the 'premium bespoke' claim.
lots.condition: Leather has an even aged patina with surface wear and some scuffing near the buckle. Stitching looks intact, and the brass fittings are present and look original but are not proven. Inside face unseen.
lots.question_for_gowans: Please show or describe the inside of the belt: is there a legible J. Fotheringham, Launceston maker's stamp, and where exactly is W H Gray's name, and is it stamped or handwritten? Who wrote the printed sheet (vendor or Gowans) and is there any documented provenance linking the belt to Gray? Is the cross strap included?
lots.dropped_entries: The researcher reported no entries. None added: WebSearch was unavailable (budget 200 of 200), and the Grays search page returned no Sam Browne listings in its static content.

lots.guide_summary: All surviving evidence is SOLD: five same-item 70cl results at Scotch Whisky Auctions, Nov 2025 to Sep 2026 (plus May 2025), all pages opened, hammer £25 to £60 (A$48 to A$114). The search pages show about 40 more single 70cl lots from Oct 2024 to Sep 2026, mostly £30 to £40 (A$57 to A$76). No unsold or asking evidence. All UK results, no Australian sales found. Rate AUD 1.907 per GBP (open.er-api.com, 1 Oct 2026; frankfurter.dev gave 1.9069 for 30 Sep 2026).
lots.working: Keep: lowest same-item SOLD in 24 months = £25 (Nov 2025) x 1.907 = A$47.68; / 1.198 = A$39.80; rounded down to $5 = $35. Flip: likely resale is the typical recent result, £35 = A$66.75 (UK hammer, used as a proxy because no Australian sale was found). Less about 15% seller's commission if resold through a local auction such as Gowans, with $0 outbound postage because the bottle is dropped off locally: 66.75 x 0.85 = A$56.74; / 2.396 = A$23.68; rounded down = $20. Flipping is marginal: about A$25 to A$30 gross margin at best. Selling liquor privately in Australia (eBay etc.) needs care, which is why local auction resale is assumed.
lots.confidence_reason: The label is read clearly and many same-item SOLD results with opened pages support a value of about A$50 to A$75. Marked down from High because the fill level and seal cannot be seen through the opaque bottle and all the evidence is from the UK, not Australia.
